title: What Is Our Calling's Glorious Hope
description: What Is Our Calling's Glorious Hope in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: John Wesley printed these words in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 406. They first appeared in a book he and his brother Charles published together, and the Collection's own index cannot say which of the two wrote them.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Metre (8.6.8.6), and this page sets them to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: What is our call-ing's glo-rious hope, But in-ward ho-li-ness? For this to Je-sus I look up, I calm-ly wait for this.

lines: What is our calling's glorious hope,
But inward holiness?
For this to Jesus I look up,
I calmly wait for this.
I wait, till he shall touch me clean,
Shall life and power impart,
Give me the faith that casts out sin,
And purifies the heart.
This is the dear redeeming grace,
For every sinner free;
Surely it shall on me take place,
The chief of sinners, me.
From all iniquity, from all,
He shall my soul redeem;
In Jesus I believe, and shall
Believe myself to him.
When Jesus makes my heart his home,
My sin shall all depart;
And lo! he saith, I quickly come,
To fill and rule thy heart!
Be it according to thy word!
Redeem me from all sin;
My heart would now receive thee, Lord,
Come in, my Lord, come in!

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788; John Wesley died in 1791.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788) or John Wesley (1703–1791), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
